recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-9855 unless a future work group decision changes Coverage beneficiary, patient, or subscriber search semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-9855 is a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Coverage change request from the Financial Management work group. It asked for Coverage to be searchable by Patient, suggested a subscriber reference search parameter, and was resolved as searchable by Beneficiary in STU3.
initial_application: No git commit or current source mention explicitly tagged FHIR-9855, #9855, or Tracker #9855 was found. The current Coverage search-parameter source already contains Coverage-beneficiary, and the source rework commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 carried both Coverage-beneficiary and Coverage-patient into the current bundle-based source layout. The later same-change-family issue FHIR-14239 explicitly added the Coverage-patient alias over Coverage.beneficiary in b0bea066a1a25eeb0da918c4729e9479d9d89908.
additional_context: Coverage is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/coverage/bundle-Coverage-search-params.xml is in current build scope. Coverage.beneficiary is a required Reference(Patient), and the current bundle defines Coverage-beneficiary over Coverage.beneficiary, Coverage-patient over Coverage.beneficiary, and Coverage-subscriber over Coverage.subscriber. FHIR-14239 is already represented on the combined branch by commit 4db6cd22acf9a940e4d66e8f370df62f843606a3.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current source already satisfies the final FHIR-9855 resolution by making Coverage searchable by beneficiary, and it also exposes the patient alias that implementers would use to retrieve coverages for a patient.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Coverage issue explicitly added a patient search parameter over Coverage.beneficiary and is already audited on the combined branch.
